findings.title: Server-only key used in browser code

cwe.name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere

findings.evidence: billing.ts runs in the browser and uses `VITE_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`.
findings.whyItMatters: Code in this file runs in the visitor's browser. A Supabase service role key or Stripe secret key there gives full control of the database or the Stripe account to anyone who opens developer tools. If it was ever deployed, treat the key as leaked.
findings.fix: Use only public keys in the browser (the Supabase anon or publishable key, the Stripe publishable key) and keep secret keys in server code. Rotate the key if this was ever deployed.
findings.subject: VITE_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY

patch.summary: Renames VITE_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY to STRIPE_SECRET_KEY in .env.example, src/lib/billing.ts.
caveats: Rename the variable in your hosting dashboard too, and rotate the key if a build with VITE_ ever went live.
patch.partial: The key is out of the browser bundle after the next build, but the code that used it still runs in the browser and now gets an empty value. Move that code to a Supabase Edge Function that reads it with `Deno.env.get()` and checks the caller's JWT, and look up whose data it may touch from the session there, never from an argument the browser sends. Until then the feature is off, which is safer than a key anyone can copy.

findings.title: Stripe webhook accepts unsigned requests
findings.evidence: Handles Stripe events without `constructEvent`, so any POST is trusted.
findings.whyItMatters: The webhook acts on whatever JSON it receives. Anyone who finds the URL can post a fake 'payment completed' event and get the paid plan for free.
findings.fix: Verify the `stripe-signature` header with `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent` on the raw request body before acting on the event.
findings.subject: constructEvent

patch.summary: Reads the raw body and checks the stripe-signature header with constructEventAsync and Stripe's SubtleCrypto provider (Deno has no Node crypto) before the function touches the event. Unsigned or tampered requests get a 400.
caveats: Set the secret: `supabase secrets set STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_...` (the endpoint's signing secret from the Stripe dashboard).
Keep `verify_jwt = false` for this function in supabase/config.toml: Stripe sends no Supabase token, and the signature is now the gate.

findings.title: Policy lets everyone through (using true)
findings.evidence: Policy "Enable read access for all users" on `public.leads` (select) lets anyone (signed in or not) read every row.
findings.whyItMatters: A policy with `using (true)` or `with check (true)` allows the action for every caller, including visitors who are not signed in. If the table holds anything private, it is public.
findings.fix: Replace the policy with one that compares `auth.uid()` to the owner column, and limit it to the `authenticated` role.

findings.title: View skips Row Level Security
findings.evidence: View `public.pipeline_summary` has no `security_invoker`, so it reads the tables below it without RLS.
findings.snippet:
23 | create view public.pipeline_summary as
  24 |   select owner_id, stage, count(*) as deals, sum(amount_cents) as total_cents
  25 |   from public.deals
  26 |   group by owner_id, stage;
findings.whyItMatters: Postgres views run with the rights of whoever created them, so they ignore the policies of the tables below. Supabase serves the view over the API, which gives every caller the rows your policies were meant to hide.
findings.fix: Set `security_invoker = true` on the view (Postgres 15+), so it runs with the caller's rights and the table policies apply.
findings.subject: public.pipeline_summary

live.summary: A visitor without an account can read 2 rows (1 of them user A's). User B can read user A's 1 row.

patch.diff:
diff --git a/supabase/migrations/20261116090001_security_invoker_pipeline_summary.sql b/supabase/migrations/20261116090001_security_invoker_pipeline_summary.sql
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/supabase/migrations/20261116090001_security_invoker_pipeline_summary.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+-- PA-04: make public.pipeline_summary respect the caller's RLS.
+-- Generated by prelaunch-audit. Review before applying.
+alter view public.pipeline_summary set (security_invoker = true);
patch.summary: Sets security_invoker on public.pipeline_summary, so the policies of the tables below it apply to whoever queries it.
caveats: Needs Postgres 15 or newer (every current Supabase project is).

findings.title: Table open to the public API (Row Level Security off)
findings.evidence: `public.invoices` is created without `enable row level security` in any migration.
findings.snippet:
1 | create table public.invoices (
   2 |   id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
   3 |   customer_id uuid not null references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
   4 |   number text not null,
findings.whyItMatters: Supabase serves every table in the public schema over its REST API, and the key it needs ships in your website. With Row Level Security off, anyone can read, change or delete every row of this table from a browser console.
findings.fix: Enable Row Level Security on the table. With no policies the API gets nothing, and your server code (service role) keeps working. Add policies only for what the browser really needs.
findings.subject: public.invoices

live.summary: A visitor without an account can read 2 rows (1 of them user A's). User B can read user A's 1 row.

patch.diff:
diff --git a/supabase/migrations/20261116090002_enable_rls_invoices.sql b/supabase/migrations/20261116090002_enable_rls_invoices.sql
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/supabase/migrations/20261116090002_enable_rls_invoices.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,8 @@
+-- PA-05: turn on Row Level Security for public.invoices.
+-- Generated by prelaunch-audit. Review before applying.
+alter table public.invoices enable row level security;
+
+create policy invoices_select_own
+  on public.invoices for select
+  to authenticated

patch.summary: Turns on Row Level Security for public.invoices and lets a signed-in user read only their own rows. The public API can no longer write it; server code using the service role key keeps working.
caveats: If the browser also inserts, updates or deletes rows here, add a policy per command with the same owner check.

findings.title: Live database lets other people read users' rows
findings.evidence: Live project, `public.open_tasks`: User B can read user A's 2 rows. This is a view: it shows what the tables under it let through (or bypasses their policies if it was made without `security_invoker`), so fix it there.
findings.whyItMatters: This was measured on the running project, not guessed from code: the probe signed in as a second test user (or as nobody) and counted rows that belong to someone else. The migrations in the repo do not explain it, so the policy or grant that lets it through was changed in the dashboard or the table was made there.
findings.fix: Run `supabase db pull` (or `supabase db diff --linked`) to get the live policies into a migration, fix the select policy so it compares the owner column with `auth.uid()`, push it, and run the live probe again.

live.summary: User B can read user A's 2 rows.

patch.diff:
diff --git a/supabase/migrations/20261116090003_restrict_select_tasks.sql b/supabase/migrations/20261116090003_restrict_select_tasks.sql
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/supabase/migrations/20261116090003_restrict_select_tasks.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+-- PA-07: only the owner can read rows of public.tasks.
+-- Generated by prelaunch-audit. Review before applying.
+-- The policy that lets this through is not in the migrations, so its name is unknown. A restrictive policy is
+-- ANDed with every permissive one, so it closes the leak whatever the dashboard policy is called.
+alter table public.tasks enable row level security;
+drop policy if exists "Only owners read tasks (restrictive)" on public.tasks;
+create policy "Only owners read tasks (restrictive)"
+  on public.tasks
+  as restrictive
+  for select
+  to anon, authenticated
+  using ((select auth.uid()) = owner_id);
patch.summary: Adds a restrictive select policy on public.tasks: a row is readable only by its owner (`owner_id`), whatever the policies made in the dashboard allow.
caveats: Owners still need a normal (permissive) select policy for their own rows. Run `supabase db pull` first to see what the live project has, and keep that in a migration too.
If some rows are meant to be shared (a team, a public profile), this blocks that as well: write the sharing rule into the policy instead.

findings.title: Other users can list files in a user's storage folder

cwe.name: Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties

findings.evidence: Live project, bucket `attachments`: User B can list 1 of the entries in user A's folder.
findings.whyItMatters: The probe listed user A's folder in this bucket as user B (or as nobody) and got entries back. A file that can be listed can usually be downloaded with the same rights, so uploads such as contracts or ID scans are open to other accounts.
findings.fix: Limit the select policy on `storage.objects` for this bucket to the owner's folder: `bucket_id = '<bucket>' and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text`. Do the same for insert, update and delete.
findings.subject: storage:attachments

live.summary: User B can list 1 of the entries in user A's folder.

patch.diff:
diff --git a/supabase/migrations/20261116090004_restrict_bucket_attachments.sql b/supabase/migrations/20261116090004_restrict_bucket_attachments.sql
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/supabase/migrations/20261116090004_restrict_bucket_attachments.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,11 @@
+-- PA-08: files in attachments are readable only from the owner's folder.
+-- Generated by prelaunch-audit. Review before applying.
+-- The policy that lets this through is not in the migrations, so its name is unknown. A restrictive policy is
+-- ANDed with every permissive one, so it closes the leak whatever the dashboard policy is called.
+drop policy if exists "Only owners read attachments files (restrictive)" on storage.objects;
+create policy "Only owners read attachments files (restrictive)"
+  on storage.objects
+  as restrictive
+  for select
+  to anon, authenticated
+  using (bucket_id <> 'attachments' or (storage.foldername(name))[1] = (select auth.uid())::text);
patch.summary: Adds a restrictive select policy on storage.objects for the attachments bucket: a file is listable and downloadable over the API only from `<your user id>/`.
caveats: Assumes files live under `<user id>/…`, the layout the live check found user A's file in. Files stored another way become unreadable.

findings.title: Users can edit their own plan or role column

cwe.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

findings.evidence: Policy "Users can update their own profile" lets users update their row in `public.profiles`, including `plan` and `stripe_customer_id`. No column privilege or trigger stops them.
findings.snippet:
17 | create policy "Users can update their own profile"
  18 |   on public.profiles for update
  19 |   to authenticated
  20 |   using (auth.uid() = id);
findings.whyItMatters: The update policy lets a signed-in user change any column of their own row, including the one that says what they paid for. One request from the browser console turns a free account into a paid one.
findings.fix: Limit what users may update with column privileges (grant update only on the safe columns) and add `with check` to the policy. Change the plan only from the server, after Stripe confirms payment.

findings.title: Privileged database function callable by anyone
findings.evidence: `public.delete_lead()` is SECURITY DEFINER and anon can call it at /rest/v1/rpc/delete_lead (Supabase's default grant was never revoked).
findings.snippet:
27 | create function public.delete_lead(lead_id uuid)
  28 | returns void
  29 | language sql
  30 | security definer
findings.whyItMatters: The function runs with its owner's rights, so it skips Row Level Security. Supabase exposes it at /rest/v1/rpc/, and visitors who are not signed in may call it.
findings.fix: Revoke execute from `public`, `anon` and `authenticated`, grant it only to the roles that need it, and check the caller inside the function.
findings.subject: public.delete_lead

patch.diff:
diff --git a/supabase/migrations/20261116090006_revoke_delete_lead.sql b/supabase/migrations/20261116090006_revoke_delete_lead.sql
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/supabase/migrations/20261116090006_revoke_delete_lead.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+-- PA-10: stop the API roles from calling public.delete_lead().
+-- Generated by prelaunch-audit. Review before applying.
+revoke execute on function public.delete_lead(lead_id uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;
patch.summary: Revokes execute on public.delete_lead() from public, anon and authenticated. The service role keeps its own grant, so server code can still call it.
caveats: Call it only from server code that has checked the user is allowed to (for an admin action: that they are an admin).

findings.title: Policy exists but lets one user reach another user's rows
findings.evidence: RLS probe on `public.deals`: user B could select 1 of 1 of user A's rows. Let through by policy "Authenticated users can view deals" (select, `using (auth.role() = 'authenticated'::text)`).
findings.whyItMatters: The table has Row Level Security and policies, so a dashboard check passes. The probe signed in as a second user and still read or changed the first user's rows: the policy checks that someone is signed in, not who owns the row.
findings.fix: Compare the owner column with `auth.uid()` in every policy on this table (`using` for reads, updates and deletes, `with check` for inserts and updates).
